newsitem.title: USA: L.A. transit agency warns of construction delays.
newsitem.headline: L.A. transit agency warns of construction delays.

text.p: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority officials warned the authority's subway construction schedule may have to be extended due to a shortfall in federal funding.
A congressional panel on Wednesday allocated $70 million for the authority's Metro Red Line project, short of the $158.9 million requested to extend the subway project.
"We recognize that we're dealing with a shrinking universe of funds, combined with increased competition for those funds," said MTA Chairman Larry Zarian.

"If this trend continues, the MTA will be concerned with the long term impacts on the schedule of rail construction," Zarian said. "It may mean...that the schedule of our construction may need to be extended."
The federal government has pledged to provide $1.4 billion for Metro Red Line extensions to North Hollywood, Mid-Cities, and East Los Angeles and to provide the funds by 2002.
MTA has received $440.7 million of the promised total, the authority said.

Joe Drew, MTA's chief executive, said the authority was in the process of updating its 20-year plan, adding that the congressional action "underscores the fact that Los Angeles cannot expect to maintain its rail construction program schedule with the funding we have received in recent years."
Drew said the authority must have assurances from Congress that it will honor its commitments.
"We must and we will face these fiscal realities," Drew said.
